# Overview

This page characterizes the single long-read RNA-seq dataset we currently have
for the stimulated-neuron project. 

# The file

```
/project/xinhe/xsun/long_read_RNA/data/NP184_NP187_NP188_combined_DUAN_21-0/
  merged.curated.minimap2.bam       27.5 GB
  merged.curated.minimap2.bam.bai   (older than the BAM — should be regenerated)
```

**Platform and chemistry**

Oxford Nanopore + 10x Chromium 3' v3, aligned with minimap2 splice, to hg38.


# Read-level summary

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total alignments | 85,465,939 |
| Primary | 61,189,011 |
| Secondary (multimappers, **retained**) | 23,879,762 |
| Supplementary | 397,166 |
| Mapped | 99.99% |
| Marked duplicates | 0 |

Two practical consequences:

- **Always filter with `-F 0x900`.** Secondary alignments are 28% of records
  and will inflate any naive count.
- The BAM is already **UMI-deduplicated** (the "curated" in the filename):
  1.01 reads per (cell barcode, UMI) pair. So primary reads ≈ UMIs.

# Cell-level QC

**8,612 cell barcodes** (= `@RG` count; 8,605 observed in a genome-wide sample).

| Per-cell metric | median | mean | p10 | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UMIs (reads) | 4,967 | 7,105 | 1,536 | 14,477 |
| % chrM | 4.2% | 6.2% | 0.5% | 14.5% |
| % spliced reads | 16.9% | 20.3% | 10.5% | 39.5% |
| mean read length | 612 | 611 | 562 | 662 |

The minimum is 508 reads/cell, so **empty droplets were already filtered
upstream**. 408 cells exceed 20% chrM; 5 exceed 50%.

# Read length and splicing

This is the single most consequential property for the isoform plan.

From a genome-wide sample of 450k primary reads across 12 windows:

- Query length: median **506 bp**, mean 624, p90 1,115, p99 2,038, max 5,963.
- Only **27.3% of reads are spliced** (contain a CIGAR `N`); among those,
  median 2 junctions, p90 6.

These are largely **3' fragments, not full-length transcripts** — expected for
a 10x 3' library, but it does undercut full-length isoform quantification.
Junction-level methods (LeafCutter-style intron clustering) are likely the more
robust route than isoform-level quantification, despite the header showing
IsoQuant was run upstream.

# Contamination and background

- **rRNA carryover is substantial.** 677k of 1.31M chr21 primary reads fall in
  the chr21:8.2–8.6 Mb rDNA array. The rDNA-bearing scaffolds `GL000220.1`
  (2.44M) and `KI270733.1` (2.52M) are also heavily loaded (those counts
  include secondary alignments).
- chrM is 3.97M mapped reads (~4.6% overall; median 4.2% per cell).
- Filter rDNA regions and chrM before quantification.

<!-- # Planned method: isoLASER -->

<!-- [Quinones-Valdez, Amoah & Xiao, *Nat Commun* 16:9603 -->
<!-- (2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64605-6). Downloaded -->
<!-- 2026-09-04 to: -->

<!-- ``` -->
<!-- /project/xinhe/xsun/long_read_RNA/software/isoLASER/        @ 7656083, tag v0.0.3 -->
<!-- /project/xinhe/xsun/long_read_RNA/software/isoLASER_paper/  (Snakemake s1-s4) -->
<!-- ``` -->

<!-- `software/isoLASER/test_pipeline/` ships real test data (3 DLPFC BAMs, expected -->
<!-- outputs, `isolaser_test.smk`), so an install can be validated end-to-end before -->
<!-- touching our data. -->

<!-- ## What it does -->

<!-- Per-sample de novo variant calling (scAllele-based de Bruijn reassembly + MLP -->
<!-- filter) → gene-level phasing (weighted k-means, **K = 2, assuming one diploid -->
<!-- genome**) → linkage test between haplotype and exonic-part inclusion, scored by -->
<!-- adjusted mutual information (AMI) with a delta-PSI ≥ 5% effect filter. Events -->
<!-- are split into **cis-directed** (AMI above the 99th percentile of a simulated -->
<!-- null) versus **trans-directed** (below the 95th). `isolaser_joint` merges ≥ 2 -->
<!-- samples to call splicing-associated variants (SAVs), and can reach rare -->
<!-- variants. -->

<!-- The attraction for aim 2: it needs neither a pre-phased genome nor a VCF, and -->
<!-- it works at small sample sizes — the paper explicitly frames it as an -->
<!-- alternative to sQTL mapping. Their SAVs replicated against GTEx sQTLs -->
<!-- (delta PSI vs sQTL beta, R = −0.37). -->

<!-- ## Compatibility with our data -->

<!-- **isoLASER expects bulk, single-donor long-read RNA-seq; our BAM is pooled -->
<!-- single-cell.** The phasing step fixes K = 2 on the assumption of one diploid -->
<!-- genome, so running it directly on 8,612 cells from ≥ 2 donors would be -->
<!-- meaningless. The correct order is: -->

<!-- > demultiplex donors → pseudobulk per donor → `isolaser` per donor → -->
<!-- > `isolaser_joint` across donors -->

<!-- Donor demultiplexing is therefore a **prerequisite, not an optional extra**. -->

<!-- Two further concerns: -->

<!-- - isoLASER needs a heterozygous SNP **and** the splicing event on the *same -->
<!--   read*, and its pipeline discards reads lacking splice junctions. With our -->
<!--   506 bp median and 27% spliced fraction, testable events per donor will be -->
<!--   well below what the full-length PacBio data the method was built on gives. -->
<!--   Worth estimating before committing. -->
<!-- - The paper's own ONT caveat: for Nanopore they "recommend focusing analyses on -->
<!--   SNPs by excluding indels and validating detected variants against external -->
<!--   datasets prior to phasing" (they required gnomAD presence). Our median error -->
<!--   (~1.1%) is better than the R9.4.1 data they used, but this still applies. -->
